top_news.title: Bounded Personas Match Retrieval on Classification but Not Regression for a Frozen Agent
top_news.dek: Distilled personas match retrieval-based methods for classification tasks but underperform in regression for frozen language agents.
top_news.brief: Researchers compared retrieval-based history management against distilled natural-language personas. While distillation offers lower latency and query independence, it struggles to maintain accuracy in regression tasks compared to retrieval, which pulls specific past interactions into the prompt.
top_news.image_alt: Comparison chart showing performance gap between retrieval and distillation methods

top_news.title: Which tools do Claude, Codex and Cursor choose? We measured 17k runs to find out
top_news.dek: An analysis of 17,000 coding agent sessions reveals how models like Claude and Cursor select third-party tools.
top_news.brief: The study examines how AI coding agents choose services and libraries when tasked with implementation. It highlights the growing influence of agents in the software supply chain, as they increasingly act as the primary decision-makers for selecting infrastructure and dependencies.
top_news.image_alt: Data visualization of tool selection frequency by AI coding agents

top_news.title: Anthropic Released Claude Commerce Agents: An Apache-2.0 Blueprint for Shopping and Merchant Agents Across Retail, Travel, Telecom and Entertainment
top_news.dek: Anthropic released an Apache-2.0 blueprint for building commerce agents across retail, travel, and telecom.
top_news.brief: The repository provides standardized scaffolding for commerce agents, including agent loops, tool layers, approval gates, and evaluation suites. It includes four runnable vertical implementations to help developers avoid rebuilding common commerce-specific infrastructure.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram of the commerce agent architecture blueprint

top_news.title: Data from drones in Ukraine is fueling a new Wild West marketplace
top_news.dek: Battlefield drone data from Ukraine is creating a new market for training AI models in defense and civilian sectors.
top_news.brief: Drones generate massive datasets of images, video, and controller inputs that capture human-machine responses to dynamic environments. This data is becoming a valuable asset for training AI architectures, raising questions about the commercialization of conflict-derived information.
top_news.image_alt: Aerial view of drone data collection process

primary.title: Equation Recast for Canonical Operator Learning Across Parametric PDEs
primary.summary: Learning solution operators across broad parameter ranges can require substantial coverage of both input functions and physical parameters, particularly for purely data-driven parametric models. In addition, the resulting models may fail silently outside the training distribution. We introduce equation recast, which reformulates parametric operator learning as the learning of a single canonical operator. Parameter-induced operator variations are derived analytically from the governing equation and absorbed into effective sources, enabling zero-shot prediction across new parameter regimes. Acro

primary.title: Counterexamples as Feedback for Agent Self-Correction
primary.summary: Single-turn code-generation metrics understate a central property of deployed agents: whether they can repair a wrong artifact after receiving concrete feedback. An agent proposes a regex, a deterministic oracle checks it under full-match semantics, and compact false-positive or false-negative witnesses guide the next turn. primary.summary: We look at zg (zvec-grep), the local-first search layer that Qwen Developers just open-sourced under Apache 2.0. We explain how it puts ripgrep, BM25, and vector search behind a single interface, so an agent can move from a plain-language description to an exact line span without switching tools.
